name: PzH 2000

key_facts.label: Protection
key_facts.value: range up to 60km with guided projectile, 40km active-reactive, 30km conventional

characteristics: range up to 60km with guided projectile, 40km active-reactive, 30km conventional
Strength: Longest range and highest rate of fire among Ukraine's donated SPGs; heavy armor protection relative to wheeled types
Limitation: Very heavy (55t+), demanding on transport and bridging infrastructure; complex to maintain
Estimated quantity available: Dozens delivered (Germany + other European donors)
employment_notes: Considered one of the most capable SPGs in the war on paper; heavy logistics footprint has limited how many can be sustained forward at once
contrast_vs_traditional: PzH 2000 was built for NATO's Cold War rate-of-fire doctrine — massed, sustained barrages from a position expected to stay concealed for the mission. Against a drone that can loiter over a firing position and hand a target to counter-battery fire within minutes, the same rate of fire that was the platform's original selling point is now also what keeps a crew in place long enough to be found.
